body_markdown:
Whether you were behind the wheel or behind a safety wall as a spectator, I reckon that many of us have a memorable story about our times at a racetrack. Maybe it was the taste of a hot dog while sitting in the bleachers, catching whiffs of nitromethane fumes from a Top Fuel dragster at an NHRA event. Or the feel of your first taste of oversteer, right before you lost control and slid off the road course during a track day.


Or anything in between, because our memories of racetracks are something to be embraced. And they should be shared, so I’m asking Hagerty Media readers to do just that. As usual, I’ll start things off with my favorite memory.


## My First Track Day


[Sajeev Mehta](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/sajeev-mehta/)


I forgot the exact year this photo was taken, but it was probably in 2005: That’s me driving my lightly modified, daily-driver 1988 Mercury Cougar XR-7 at Motorsport Ranch in Houston, TX.


I was but a college student with a Fox Body sporting blown-out Monroe VST shocks. The rest of the car was in good shape, and I learned from the internet that an extra quart of oil eliminated starvation during sustained cornering at high speed. So I scrounged up the cash for an entry fee, grabbed another quart of 10w-30, and hit the track with no instructor.


I had no clue how I’d fare against other novice drivers out there. Turns out I was the fastest novice by a huge margin: C5 and C6 Corvettes ate my dust on MSR’s high-speed carousel, as massive body roll at full throttle ensured I earned a coveted “point by” signal. Perhaps the others were less concerned with extracting the most from their vehicles. Or maybe they were more concerned about getting that 17-year-old Cougar out of their rear-view mirror whenever they needed to slow down for a corner?


No matter, adding the extra quart of oil helped, as did locking Ford’s AOD transmission out of overdrive. I did boil my brake fluid, but the Cougar still stopped with authority with its four-wheel discs derived from other Ford vehicles. I was the outlier in my group, and the track staff initially didn’t pay me any attention.


But that all changed, as many a staffer smiled when the Cougar exited after its final run. And that might be the best part of my first time on track. So I ask the question again: **What’s Your Favorite Race Track Experience?**
